inverse_equation.name: Exact Analytical Inverse Rubber-Band Transformation
inverse_equation.asymptotic_singularity_guard: To avoid division by zero and unconstrained negative divergence when abs(x_rubber) >= d, visual overscroll is clamped to abs(x_rubber) <= 0.9999 * d
inverse_equation.role: Reconstructs unconstrained touch centroid displacement from current visual overscroll offset for gesture reconciliation and velocity preservation

zoom_rubber_band_equation.name: Logarithmic Zoom Scale Damping Function
zoom_rubber_band_equation.below_min_formula: s_rubber = s_min - ln(1.0 + (s_min - s) / s_min) * c_zoom * s_min
zoom_rubber_band_equation.above_max_formula: s_rubber = s_max + ln(1.0 + (s - s_max) / s_max) * c_zoom * s_max
zoom_rubber_band_equation.degenerate_input_guard: Proposed scale is clamped to s >= 0.0 and output bounded to s_rubber >= s_min * (1.0 - ln(2.0) * c_zoom) ~ 0.8267 * s_min > 0.0 to prevent inverted coordinate transform matrices
zoom_rubber_band_equation.role: Modulates pinch gesture scaling beyond minimumZoomScale and maximumZoomScale

primary_drag_resistance_c.description: Standard dimensionless overscroll drag resistance coefficient across touch interactions

touch_finger.description: Standard capacitive finger touch rubber-banding coefficient

large_trackpad.description: Large external Magic Trackpad rubber-banding coefficient

mouse_wheel_continuous.description: Smooth continuous scroll wheel rubber-banding coefficient

dimension_parameter_d.physical_definition: Visible viewport dimension along the active scroll axis (bounds.size)
dimension_parameter_d.scale_invariance_proof: Normalizing by viewport dimension d guarantees scale invariance: dragging 100pt past boundary yields identical visual compression percentage across iPhones, iPads, and Mac Catalyst windows

instruction_sequence: 0x184ae00dc: fsub d0, d0, d10      ; delta = offset - bound (x)
0x184ae00e0: fdiv d0, d0, d1        ; x / d
0x184ae00e4: adrp x8, 0x186516000   ; load page containing c
0x184ae00ec: fmul d0, d0, d2        ; (x / d) * c
0x184ae0104: fadd d10, d10, d0      ; bound + x_rubber
0x184b1e5fc: fsub d0, d0, d1        ; delta = offset - minBound
0x184b1e604: fdiv d0, d0, d2        ; x / d
0x184b1e610: fmul d0, d0, d3        ; (x / d) * c
0x184b1e628: fadd d9, d1, d0        ; bound + x_rubber

axis_symmetry_and_rules.horizontal_symmetry: Strictly symmetric: left and right overscroll share identical coefficient c = 0.55 and formula
axis_symmetry_and_rules.vertical_symmetry: Strictly symmetric: top and bottom overscroll share identical coefficient c = 0.55 and formula
axis_symmetry_and_rules.axis_decoupling: Horizontal and vertical axes are evaluated completely independently; a diagonal drag decomposes into independent orthogonal rubber-band evaluations
axis_symmetry_and_rules.boundary_asymmetry: While the resistance curve is symmetric, boundary values minOffset and maxOffset are asymmetric due to contentInset and safeAreaInsets differences

evaluated_models.rejection_reason: exp() function introduces transcendental math library call overhead and non-linear rounding divergences on floating point units
tanh() requires transcendental evaluation and saturates too rapidly for large displacements
